motivation_short: for developing semiconductor heterostructures used in high-speed- and opto-electronics
discovery_work: H. Kroemer, 'Quasi-electric and quasi-magnetic fields in nonuniform semiconductors', RCA Review 18, 332 (1957); companion paper H. Kroemer, 'Theory of a wide-gap emitter for transistors', Proc. IRE 45, 1535 (1957) (heterojunction bipolar transistor)
realization_work: Zh. I. Alferov et al., 'Investigation of the influence of the AlAs-GaAs heterostructure parameters on the laser threshold current and the realization of continuous emission at room temperature', Fiz. Tekh. Poluprovodn. 4, 1826 (1970) [Sov. Phys. Semicond. 4, 1573 (1971)]
note: The committee credits 'the main analysis and suggestions' on heterojunction transistors to Kroemer at RCA in 1957 (graded gap, quasi-electric fields), plus his DH-laser proposal, Proc. IEEE 51, 1782 (1963). Kroemer's Nobel lecture calls the 1957 RCA Review paper (1957a, first given at the April 1957 Brooklyn symposium) the first statement of the general heterostructure design principle. A precursor graded-gap-base idea appears in Archiv d. Elekt. Übertragung 8, 499 (1954). Realization is shared with Alferov's half (the first CW room-temperature DH laser, 1970).

motivation_short: for his part in the invention of the integrated circuit
discovery_work: J. S. Kilby, 'Semiconductor solid circuits', Electronics 32 (7 Aug 1959), pp. 110-111 (first publication); patent US 3,138,743 'Miniaturized electronic circuits', filed 6 Feb 1959, issued 23 Jun 1964
realization_work: Same as discovery: Kilby built the first working integrated circuit himself (germanium oscillator, demonstrated 12 Sep 1958), first described publicly in Electronics 32, 110 (1959)
note: The committee describes the summer/September 1958 demonstration and the 6 Feb 1959 patent application, and cites Kilby's own account, IEEE Trans. Electron Devices 23, 648 (1976). The invention and demonstration were in 1958; the first publication was in 1959. The Electronics 1959 reference comes from the Computer History Museum page.

motivation_short: for developing semiconductor heterostructures used in high-speed- and opto-electronics
discovery_work: Zh. I. Alferov & R. F. Kazarinov, 'Semiconductor laser with electric pumping', USSR Inventor's Certificate No. 181737 (application No. 950840, priority 30 Mar 1963): the double-heterostructure (DH) laser proposal
realization_work: Zh. I. Alferov, V. M. Andreev, D. Z. Garbuzov, Yu. V. Zhilyaev, E. P. Morozov, E. L. Portnoi, V. G. Trofim, 'Investigation of the influence of the AlAs-GaAs heterostructure parameters on the laser threshold current and the realization of continuous emission at room temperature', Fiz. Tekh. Poluprovodn. 4, 1826 (1970) [Sov. Phys. Semicond. 4, 1573 (1971)]
note: The committee says the DH-laser principle was suggested in 1963 by Kroemer (in a journal) and independently by Alferov & Kazarinov (in a patent application). The discovery anchor is a patent application, not a journal paper; 1963 is its priority year. Alferov's first journal paper on the DH idea is Alferov, Khalfin & Kazarinov, Fiz. Tverd. Tela 8, 3102 (1966) (superinjection). Realization chosen as the first room-temperature continuous-wave (CW) DH laser, which the committee treats as the endpoint 'from the concept in 1963 to the first continuously operating lasers in 1970'. Alferov's group submitted it in May 1970; Bell Labs' Hayashi, Panish, Foy & Sumski, Appl. Phys. Lett. 17, 109 (1970), submitted in June 1970, may have appeared in print first. Earlier lasing: GaAsP DH at 77 K, Sov. Phys. Solid State 9, 208 (1967); pulsed AlGaAs DH, Fiz. Tekh. Poluprovodn. 2, 1545 (1968) (the committee's 'late 1968'). Use 1968 if the earliest DH lasing is wanted instead.

motivation_short: for the achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms, and for early fundamental studies of the properties of the condensates
discovery_work: M. H. Anderson, J. R. Ensher, M. R. Matthews, C. E. Wieman, E. A. Cornell, 'Observation of Bose-Einstein condensation in a dilute atomic vapor', Science 269, 198 (1995)
realization_work: M. H. Anderson, J. R. Ensher, M. R. Matthews, C. E. Wieman, E. A. Cornell, 'Observation of Bose-Einstein condensation in a dilute atomic vapor', Science 269, 198 (1995)
note: Shared with Cornell, as co-authors of the same paper. The committee credits Wieman with the strategy (laser-cool in a MOT, magnetic trap, evaporative cooling): Monroe, Swann, Robinson & Wieman, PRL 65, 1571 (1990).

motivation_short: for the achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms, and for early fundamental studies of the properties of the condensates
discovery_work: M. H. Anderson, J. R. Ensher, M. R. Matthews, C. E. Wieman, E. A. Cornell, 'Observation of Bose-Einstein condensation in a dilute atomic vapor', Science 269, 198 (1995)
realization_work: M. H. Anderson, J. R. Ensher, M. R. Matthews, C. E. Wieman, E. A. Cornell, 'Observation of Bose-Einstein condensation in a dilute atomic vapor', Science 269, 198 (1995)
note: This is an experimental discovery, so discovery = realization (87Rb BEC, June 1995). Enabling steps cited by the committee: Cornell's TOP trap, Petrich et al., PRL 74, 3352 (1995); Wieman's laser-cooling route, Monroe et al., PRL 65, 1571 (1990).

motivation_short: for the achievement of Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms, and for early fundamental studies of the properties of the condensates
discovery_work: K. B. Davis, M.-O. Mewes, M. R. Andrews, N. J. van Druten, D. S. Durfee, D. M. Kurn, W. Ketterle, 'Bose-Einstein condensation in a gas of sodium atoms', Phys. Rev. Lett. 75, 3969 (1995)
realization_work: M. H. Anderson, J. R. Ensher, M. R. Matthews, C. E. Wieman, E. A. Cornell, 'Observation of Bose-Einstein condensation in a dilute atomic vapor', Science 269, 198 (1995)
note: This is Ketterle's own first BEC paper (23Na, published about 4 months after JILA's, per the committee). The first realization of the shared discovery is the JILA Science paper by his co-laureates. Precursor: optically plugged trap, Ketterle et al., PRL 70, 2253 (1993).

motivation_short: for pioneering contributions to astrophysics, in particular for the detection of cosmic neutrinos
discovery_work: K. Hirata et al. (Kamiokande-II, incl. M. Koshiba), 'Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A', Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 1490 (1987)
realization_work: R. Davis Jr., D. S. Harmer, K. C. Hoffman, 'Search for neutrinos from the Sun', Phys. Rev. Lett. 20, 1205 (1968)
note: This is Koshiba's own first detection of cosmic neutrinos (SN1987A, also the first detection of supernova neutrinos). His directional real-time confirmation of solar neutrinos is Hirata et al., PRL 63, 16 (1989). The realization is the first detection of cosmic neutrinos in the shared half, by co-laureate Davis. Use 1987 instead if Koshiba's own observation is wanted as the realization.

motivation_short: for pioneering contributions to astrophysics, in particular for the detection of cosmic neutrinos
discovery_work: R. Davis Jr., D. S. Harmer, K. C. Hoffman, 'Search for neutrinos from the Sun', Phys. Rev. Lett. 20, 1205 (1968)
realization_work: R. Davis Jr., D. S. Harmer, K. C. Hoffman, 'Search for neutrinos from the Sun', Phys. Rev. Lett. 20, 1205 (1968)
note: First Homestake chlorine results; the committee says 'Davis discovered solar neutrinos'. Earlier Davis papers: the reactor experiment, Phys. Rev. 97, 766 (1955), and the experiment proposal, PRL 12, 303 (1964), both cited.

motivation_short: for pioneering contributions to astrophysics, which have led to the discovery of cosmic X-ray sources
discovery_work: R. Giacconi, H. Gursky, F. R. Paolini, B. B. Rossi, 'Evidence for X rays from sources outside the solar system', Phys. Rev. Lett. 9, 439 (1962)
realization_work: R. Giacconi, H. Gursky, F. R. Paolini, B. B. Rossi, 'Evidence for X rays from sources outside the solar system', Phys. Rev. Lett. 9, 439 (1962)
note: Discovery of Sco X-1 and the X-ray background (rocket flight of 18 Jun 1962). An earlier instrument proposal, also cited, is the focusing X-ray telescope of Giacconi & Rossi, J. Geophys. Res. 65, 773 (1960).

motivation_short: for pioneering contributions to the theory of superconductors and superfluids
discovery_work: A. A. Abrikosov, 'On the magnetic properties of superconductors of the second group', Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 32, 1442 (1957) [Sov. Phys. JETP 5, 1174 (1957)]
realization_work: D. Cribier, B. Jacrot, L. Madhav Rao, B. Farnoux, 'Mise en evidence par diffraction de neutrons d'une structure periodique du champ magnetique dans le niobium supraconducteur', Phys. Lett. 9, 106 (1964)
note: The vortex-lattice and type-II theory, derived in 1953 and published in 1957 (the committee calls it 'groundbreaking'). Abrikosov's earlier Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 86, 489 (1952) introduced 'superconductors of the second group' from thin-film critical fields. The committee's figure credits the first pictures of the vortex lattice to U. Essmann & H. Träuble, Phys. Lett. A 24, 526 (1967). Abrikosov's Nobel lecture says the lattice was observed first by neutron diffraction (Cribier et al. 1964), then by decoration (1967). Use 1967 if only the committee-cited observation is wanted.

motivation_short: for pioneering contributions to the theory of superconductors and superfluids
discovery_work: A. J. Leggett, 'Interpretation of recent results on He3 below 3 mK: a new liquid phase?', Phys. Rev. Lett. 29, 1227 (1972)
realization_work: D. D. Osheroff & W. F. Brinkman, 'Longitudinal resonance and domain effects in the A and B phases of liquid He3', Phys. Rev. Lett. 32, 584 (1974)
note: The committee dates the 'theoretical discovery' of simultaneously broken symmetries (spontaneously broken spin-orbit symmetry) to 1972. It says Leggett's spin-dynamics predictions were confirmed, including the longitudinal NMR resonance, but gives no reference; Osheroff & Brinkman 1974 is the first observation. The experiments Leggett interpreted predate his theory: Osheroff, Richardson & Lee, PRL 28, 885 (1972) and Osheroff, Gully, Richardson & Lee, PRL 29, 920 (1972). Use 1972 if the observation of superfluid 3He itself is wanted. Earlier theory: Leggett, Phys. Rev. 140, A1869 (1965).

motivation_short: for pioneering contributions to the theory of superconductors and superfluids
discovery_work: V. L. Ginzburg & L. D. Landau, 'On the theory of superconductivity', Zh. Eksp. Teor. Fiz. 20, 1064 (1950)
realization_work: N. V. Zavaritskii, 'Critical magnetic fields of superconducting tin films', Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 78, 665 (1951)
note: Pure theory. The committee says the GL predictions on thin-film critical fields 'could soon be tested experimentally with positive results' and names Zavaritskii as verifying the dependence on film thickness and temperature, without giving a reference. The citation comes from the OSTI/ETDE record, and Abrikosov's lecture confirms the agreement. Microscopic derivation: Gor'kov 1959 (theory, not an experiment).

motivation_short: for the discovery of asymptotic freedom in the theory of the strong interaction
discovery_work: D. J. Gross & F. Wilczek, 'Ultraviolet behavior of non-abelian gauge theories', Phys. Rev. Lett. 30, 1343 (1973)
realization_work: TASSO Collaboration (R. Brandelik et al.), 'Evidence for planar events in e+e- annihilation at high energies', Phys. Lett. B 86, 243 (1979) [PETRA three-jet/gluon events; also MARK-J, D. P. Barber et al., PRL 43, 830 (1979)]
note: Pure theory. Experimental support listed by the committee: SLAC scaling, which predates the theory (Bloom et al. and Breidenbach et al., PRL 23, 930 and 935 (1969)) and which Gross, Wilczek and Politzer 'very quickly checked'; the ADONE colour factor (early 1970s); PETRA three-jet events 'observed for the first time' in the late 1970s; and the running of alpha_s (LEP compilations). Chosen: the first post-1973 confirmation the committee explicitly describes. Use 1969 if the scaling observation the theory explained is wanted.

motivation_short: for the discovery of asymptotic freedom in the theory of the strong interaction
discovery_work: D. J. Gross & F. Wilczek, 'Ultraviolet behavior of non-abelian gauge theories', Phys. Rev. Lett. 30, 1343 (1973)
realization_work: TASSO Collaboration (R. Brandelik et al.), 'Evidence for planar events in e+e- annihilation at high energies', Phys. Lett. B 86, 243 (1979) [also MARK-J, PRL 43, 830 (1979)]
note: Shared with Gross, as co-authors of the same paper. Follow-up QCD proposal: Gross & Wilczek, Phys. Rev. D 8, 3633 (1973).

motivation_short: for the discovery of asymptotic freedom in the theory of the strong interaction
discovery_work: H. D. Politzer, 'Reliable perturbative results for strong interactions?', Phys. Rev. Lett. 30, 1346 (1973)
realization_work: TASSO Collaboration (R. Brandelik et al.), 'Evidence for planar events in e+e- annihilation at high energies', Phys. Lett. B 86, 243 (1979) [also MARK-J, PRL 43, 830 (1979)]
note: Published back-to-back with Gross & Wilczek (PRL 30, issue of 25 Jun 1973). The realization anchor is shared; see Gross's row for alternatives.

motivation_short: for their contributions to the development of laser-based precision spectroscopy, including the optical frequency comb technique
discovery_work: S. A. Diddams, D. J. Jones, L.-S. Ma, S. T. Cundiff, J. L. Hall, 'Optical frequency measurement across a 104-THz gap with a femtosecond laser frequency comb', Opt. Lett. 25, 186 (2000)
realization_work: Th. Udem, J. Reichert, R. Holzwarth, T. W. Hänsch, 'Absolute optical frequency measurement of the cesium D1 line with a mode-locked laser', Phys. Rev. Lett. 82, 3568 (1999)
note: Anchored on the frequency comb named in the motivation. This is Hall's group's first comb paper (Feb 2000, committee ref [36]). His key contribution, which the committee says he was 'first to demonstrate', is the self-referenced comb: D. J. Jones et al., Science 288, 635 (2000). Hall's earlier laser-spectroscopy work cited by the committee includes Evenson et al., PRL 29, 1346 (1972) and the joint Hall & Hänsch paper, Opt. Lett. 9, 502 (1984), called a 'crucial step'; his stabilized-laser saturated absorption goes back to Barger & Hall, PRL 22, 4 (1969). A broad 'precision spectroscopy' reading would put Hall's anchor around 1969-72. The realization is shared with Hänsch (the first comb-based absolute optical frequency measurement).

motivation_short: for his contribution to the quantum theory of optical coherence
discovery_work: R. J. Glauber, 'Photon correlations', Phys. Rev. Lett. 10, 84 (1963)
realization_work: H. J. Kimble, M. Dagenais, L. Mandel, 'Photon antibunching in resonance fluorescence', Phys. Rev. Lett. 39, 691 (1977)
note: The committee says 'the correct theory was published by Roy Glauber in 1963 [PRL 10, 84]'; the full papers are Phys. Rev. 130, 2529 and 131, 2766 (1963). Pure theory. The committee names antibunching as an observable, purely quantum effect but cites no experiment; Kimble, Dagenais & Mandel 1977 is the first observation. An earlier check of coherent versus thermal photon statistics, also semiclassically explainable, is F. T. Arecchi, PRL 15, 912 (1965). Hanbury Brown-Twiss (1956) predates the theory. Use 0 for strict committee-citation-only coding.

motivation_short: for their contributions to the development of laser-based precision spectroscopy, including the optical frequency comb technique
discovery_work: J. N. Eckstein, A. I. Ferguson, T. W. Hänsch, 'High-resolution two-photon spectroscopy with picosecond light pulses', Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 847 (1978)
realization_work: Th. Udem, J. Reichert, R. Holzwarth, T. W. Hänsch, 'Absolute optical frequency measurement of the cesium D1 line with a mode-locked laser', Phys. Rev. Lett. 82, 3568 (1999)
note: The committee says the 1978 paper 'was thus the starting point in the development of frequency comb techniques'. Precursor (multiple-pulse excitation): Teets, Eckstein & Hänsch, PRL 38, 760 (1977). Earlier Hänsch laser spectroscopy: resolving the hydrogen Lamb shift with Schawlow (1972). The committee's realization reference [33] is the 1999 Cs D1 measurement; follow-ups are Opt. Lett. 24, 881 (1999) and, for self-referencing, PRL 85, 2264 (2000).

motivation_short: for their discovery of the blackbody form and anisotropy of the cosmic microwave background radiation
discovery_work: G. F. Smoot et al., 'Structure in the COBE differential microwave radiometer first-year maps', Astrophys. J. 396, L1 (1992)
realization_work: G. F. Smoot et al., 'Structure in the COBE differential microwave radiometer first-year maps', Astrophys. J. 396, L1 (1992)
note: The anisotropy part (Smoot was the DMR PI; Mather is a co-author). This is an experimental discovery, so discovery = realization. Smoot's earlier dipole anisotropy, which is not the primordial anisotropy awarded, is Smoot, Gorenstein & Muller, PRL 39, 898 (1977). Use Mather et al. 1990 if one shared COBE anchor is required for the joint prize.

motivation_short: for their discovery of the blackbody form and anisotropy of the cosmic microwave background radiation
discovery_work: J. C. Mather et al., 'A preliminary measurement of the cosmic microwave background spectrum by the Cosmic Background Explorer (COBE) satellite', Astrophys. J. 354, L37 (1990)
realization_work: J. C. Mather et al., 'A preliminary measurement of the cosmic microwave background spectrum by the Cosmic Background Explorer (COBE) satellite', Astrophys. J. 354, L37 (1990)
note: The blackbody-form part (Mather was COBE PI and FIRAS PI). This is an experimental discovery, so discovery = realization. Smoot is a co-author (COBE science team). Final FIRAS temperature: Mather et al., ApJ 512, 511 (1999).

motivation_short: for the discovery of Giant Magnetoresistance
discovery_work: M. N. Baibich, J. M. Broto, A. Fert, F. Nguyen Van Dau, F. Petroff, P. Etienne, G. Creuzet, A. Friederich, J. Chazelas, 'Giant magnetoresistance of (001)Fe/(001)Cr magnetic superlattices', Phys. Rev. Lett. 61, 2472 (1988)
realization_work: M. N. Baibich et al., 'Giant magnetoresistance of (001)Fe/(001)Cr magnetic superlattices', Phys. Rev. Lett. 61, 2472 (1988)
note: The committee says 'in 1988 two research groups independently discovered' GMR. This is an experimental discovery, so discovery = realization; it is the first GMR paper in print (21 Nov 1988).

motivation_short: for the discovery of Giant Magnetoresistance
discovery_work: G. Binasch, P. Grünberg, F. Saurenbach, W. Zinn, 'Enhanced magnetoresistance in layered magnetic structures with antiferromagnetic interlayer exchange', Phys. Rev. B 39, 4828 (1989)
realization_work: M. N. Baibich et al. (Fert group), 'Giant magnetoresistance of (001)Fe/(001)Cr magnetic superlattices', Phys. Rev. Lett. 61, 2472 (1988)
note: Grünberg's paper was received on 31 May 1988, before Fert's submission, but published on 1 Mar 1989. He also patented GMR in 1988, as the committee notes. Precursor: antiferromagnetic Fe/Cr/Fe interlayer coupling, Grünberg et al., PRL 57, 2442 (1986). The realization is the first published GMR observation in the shared prize, by co-laureate Fert.

motivation_short: for the discovery of the origin of the broken symmetry which predicts the existence of at least three families of quarks in nature
discovery_work: M. Kobayashi & T. Maskawa, 'CP-violation in the renormalizable theory of weak interaction', Prog. Theor. Phys. 49, 652 (1973)
realization_work: S. W. Herb et al., 'Observation of a dimuon resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV proton-nucleus collisions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 39, 252 (1977)
note: Submitted 1 Sep 1972, published Feb 1973. The realization is the first experimental evidence for a third quark family (the b quark/Upsilon), cited by the committee as ref [79]. The top quark followed in 1995. The KM CP-violation pattern was confirmed in B mesons by BaBar (PRL 87, 091801) and Belle (PRL 87, 091802) in 2001; the committee cites their 2002 sin2beta papers. Use 2001 if confirmation of the CP-violation mechanism itself is wanted. CP violation was already observed in 1964 (Christenson et al.), before the theory.

motivation_short: for the discovery of the origin of the broken symmetry which predicts the existence of at least three families of quarks in nature
discovery_work: M. Kobayashi & T. Maskawa, 'CP-violation in the renormalizable theory of weak interaction', Prog. Theor. Phys. 49, 652 (1973)
realization_work: S. W. Herb et al., 'Observation of a dimuon resonance at 9.5 GeV in 400-GeV proton-nucleus collisions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 39, 252 (1977)
note: Shared with Kobayashi, as co-authors of the same paper; see Kobayashi's row for the 2001 B-factory alternative.

motivation_short: for the discovery of the mechanism of spontaneous broken symmetry in subatomic physics
discovery_work: Y. Nambu, 'Axial vector current conservation in weak interactions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 4, 380 (1960)
note: This is the first published application of spontaneous symmetry breaking to particle physics (committee ref [38]; also the 1960 Purdue talk, ref [44]). Spontaneous symmetry breaking in field-theoretic BCS: Nambu, Phys. Rev. 117, 648 (1960). Canonical model: Nambu & Jona-Lasinio, Phys. Rev. 122, 345 (1961). Pure theory: the committee cites no specific experimental confirmation, only that soft-pion results 'agreed with the experimental data' and that LEP data support a spontaneously broken gauge theory, so the realization is left empty. The pion predates the theory, and the 2012 Higgs observation came after this prize.

motivation_short: groundbreaking achievements concerning the transmission of light in fibers for optical communication
discovery_work: K. C. Kao & G. A. Hockham, 'Dielectric-fibre surface waveguides for optical frequencies', Proc. IEE 113(7), 1151-1158 (1966), doi:10.1049/piee.1966.0189
realization_work: F. P. Kapron, D. B. Keck & R. D. Maurer (Corning), 'Radiation losses in glass optical waveguides', Appl. Phys. Lett. 17(10), 423-425 (1970), doi:10.1063/1.1653255
note: Prize split 2009: 1/2 Kao (fibre), 1/4 + 1/4 Boyle & Smith (CCD). The realization was by people who are not laureates (Corning). The committee cites it as the first fused-silica fibre with the low loss Kao had predicted (about 20 dB/km). Kao's own loss measurements on fused silica: Kao & Davies, J. Sci. Instrum. 1, 1063 (1968).

motivation_short: invention of an imaging semiconductor circuit - the CCD sensor
discovery_work: W. S. Boyle & G. E. Smith, 'Charge Coupled Semiconductor Devices', Bell Syst. Tech. J. 49(4), 587-593 (1970), doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1970.tb01790.x
realization_work: G. F. Amelio, M. F. Tompsett & G. E. Smith, 'Experimental Verification of the Charge Coupled Device Concept', Bell Syst. Tech. J. 49(4), 593-600 (1970), doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1970.tb01791.x
note: Shared with Boyle. Smith is a co-author of both papers in the same April 1970 issue.

motivation_short: invention of an imaging semiconductor circuit - the CCD sensor
discovery_work: W. S. Boyle & G. E. Smith, 'Charge Coupled Semiconductor Devices', Bell Syst. Tech. J. 49(4), 587-593 (1970), doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1970.tb01790.x
realization_work: G. F. Amelio, M. F. Tompsett & G. E. Smith, 'Experimental Verification of the Charge Coupled Device Concept', Bell Syst. Tech. J. 49(4), 593-600 (1970), doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1970.tb01791.x
note: Shared with Smith (1/4 each). The CCD was conceived on 17 Oct 1969. The committee calls these 'the first two papers, one theoretical and one experimental', in the same April 1970 BSTJ issue.

motivation_short: groundbreaking experiments regarding the two-dimensional material graphene
discovery_work: K. S. Novoselov, A. K. Geim, S. V. Morozov, D. Jiang, Y. Zhang, S. V. Dubonos, I. V. Grigorieva & A. A. Firsov, 'Electric Field Effect in Atomically Thin Carbon Films', Science 306(5696), 666-669 (2004), doi:10.1126/science.1102896
realization_work: Same paper: Novoselov et al., 'Electric Field Effect in Atomically Thin Carbon Films', Science 306, 666-669 (2004), doi:10.1126/science.1102896
note: An experimental prize: the 2004 paper (isolation plus field effect) is itself the first realization. Committee follow-ups: single-layer transport, Novoselov et al., PNAS 102, 10451 (2005); anomalous quantum Hall effect, Novoselov et al., Nature 438, 197 (2005) and Zhang et al., Nature 438, 201 (2005). Graphene theory goes back to Wallace (1947).

motivation_short: groundbreaking experiments regarding the two-dimensional material graphene
discovery_work: K. S. Novoselov, A. K. Geim, S. V. Morozov, D. Jiang, Y. Zhang, S. V. Dubonos, I. V. Grigorieva & A. A. Firsov, 'Electric Field Effect in Atomically Thin Carbon Films', Science 306(5696), 666-669 (2004), doi:10.1126/science.1102896
realization_work: Same paper: Novoselov et al., 'Electric Field Effect in Atomically Thin Carbon Films', Science 306, 666-669 (2004), doi:10.1126/science.1102896
note: Shared with Geim. The discovery paper is itself the first realization.

motivation_short: discovery of the accelerating expansion of the Universe through observations of distant supernovae
discovery_work: A. G. Riess et al. (High-z Supernova Search Team), 'Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant', Astron. J. 116(3), 1009-1038 (1998), doi:10.1086/300499
realization_work: Same paper: Riess et al., Astron. J. 116, 1009-1038 (1998), doi:10.1086/300499
note: Prize 1/4. Riess is first author; the committee says the analysis of the 16 SNe Ia was 'mainly analyzed by Adam Riess'.

motivation_short: discovery of the accelerating expansion of the Universe through observations of distant supernovae
discovery_work: A. G. Riess, ..., B. P. Schmidt et al. (High-z Supernova Search Team), 'Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant', Astron. J. 116(3), 1009-1038 (1998), doi:10.1086/300499
realization_work: Same paper: Riess et al., Astron. J. 116, 1009-1038 (1998), doi:10.1086/300499 (first published observation of the acceleration)
note: Prize 1/4. Schmidt founded and led the High-z team in 1994 and is a co-author. The SCP's matching result: Perlmutter et al., ApJ 517, 565 (1999).

motivation_short: discovery of the accelerating expansion of the Universe through observations of distant supernovae
discovery_work: S. Perlmutter et al. (Supernova Cosmology Project), 'Measurements of Ω and Λ from 42 High-Redshift Supernovae', Astrophys. J. 517(2), 565-586 (1999), doi:10.1086/307221
realization_work: A. G. Riess et al. (High-z Supernova Search Team, incl. B. P. Schmidt), 'Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant', Astron. J. 116(3), 1009-1038 (1998), doi:10.1086/300499
note: Prize 1/2 Perlmutter. The committee names Riess 1998 [27] and Perlmutter 1999 [28] as 'the two breakthrough papers'. Because the discovery is observational, realization is the first published observation (High-z team, Sep 1998), shared by all three laureates. The SCP paper was submitted in Sep 1998 and published in Jun 1999. Perlmutter et al., Nature 391, 51 (1998) is the paper Li et al. 2019 list, but the committee says the early-1998 papers only pointed to low matter density.
source: https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/advanced-physicsprize2011.pdf ; cross-check Li et al. 2019 prize-winning paper record https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/6NJ5RN

motivation_short: ground-breaking experimental methods that enable measuring and manipulation of individual quantum systems
discovery_work: D. J. Wineland, R. E. Drullinger & F. L. Walls, 'Radiation-Pressure Cooling of Bound Resonant Absorbers', Phys. Rev. Lett. 40, 1639-1642 (1978), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.1639
realization_work: C. Monroe, D. M. Meekhof, B. E. King, W. M. Itano & D. J. Wineland, 'Demonstration of a Fundamental Quantum Logic Gate', Phys. Rev. Lett. 75, 4714-4717 (1995), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.4714
note: A methods prize (trapped ions), so these picks are a judgement. Discovery is the first laser cooling of trapped ions, Wineland's first experiment in the committee's account; the proposal was Wineland & Dehmelt, Bull. Am. Phys. Soc. 20, 637 (1975), an abstract only. Realization is the step the committee calls a 'breakthrough': moving a superposition between the ion's internal and motional states, i.e. the first two-qubit gate (also stressed in the popular information and the ceremony speech). Intermediate steps: single Mg+ ion, Wineland & Itano, Phys. Lett. A 82, 75 (1981); quantum jumps, Bergquist et al., PRL 57, 1699 (1986); cooling to the ground state, Diedrich et al., PRL 62, 403 (1989). Cat state: Monroe et al., Science 272, 1131 (1996). Li et al. 2019 list 1995-96 papers.

discovery_work: P. Goy, J. M. Raimond, M. Gross & S. Haroche, 'Observation of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Atom Spontaneous Emission', Phys. Rev. Lett. 50, 1903-1906 (1983), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.1903

discovery_work: J. M. Kosterlitz & D. J. Thouless, 'Long range order and metastability in two dimensional solids and superfluids. (Application of dislocation theory)', J. Phys. C: Solid State Phys. 5(11), L124-L126 (1972), doi:10.1088/0022-3719/5/11/002

motivation_short: decisive contributions to the LIGO detector and the observation of gravitational waves

His contribution was leadership: LIGO director from 1994 (until 2005), creator of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration in 1997, and the plan to build Initial LIGO and then Advanced LIGO. Weiss, 'LIGO and the Detection of Gravitational Waves', Physics Today 52(10), 44 (1999).

It calls Peebles' solo paper, The Black-Body Radiation Content of the Universe and the Formation of Galaxies, ApJ 142, 1317 (submitted Mar, published Nov 1965), the starting point of physical cosmology. Later anchors and their confirmations: Peebles & Yu, ApJ 162, 815 (1970), acoustic peaks (confirmed by BOOMERanG/MAXIMA, 2000). Peebles, ApJ 263, L1 (1982), cold dark matter with dT/T ~ 5e-6 (confirmed by COBE, Smoot et al., ApJ 396, L1, 1992). Peebles, ApJ 284, 439 (1984), cosmological constant. realization_work: A. Eckart, R. Genzel, Observations of stellar proper motions near the Galactic Centre, Nature 383, 415 (1996)

These are the first NTT/SHARP stellar proper motions giving the v ~ r^-1/2 signature of a ~2.5e6 Msun point mass; extended in Eckart & Genzel, MNRAS 284, 576 (1997). realization_work: M. Miyoshi, J. Moran, J. Herrnstein, L. Greenhill, N. Nakai, P. Diamond, M. Inoue, Evidence for a black hole from high rotation velocities in a sub-parsec region of NGC4258, Nature 373, 127 (1995)

The committee names Frankignoul & Hasselmann, Tellus 29, 289 (1977) as the first application of the stochastic model to climate data. motivation_short: for the physical modelling of Earth's climate, quantifying variability and reliably predicting global warming

realization_work: G.C. Hegerl, H. von Storch, K. Hasselmann, B.D. Santer, U. Cubasch, P.D. Jones, Detecting Greenhouse-Gas-Induced Climate Change with an Optimal Fingerprint Method, J. Climate 9, 2281 (1996)

Dyn. 13, 613 (1997). DOIs: 10.1175/1520-0469(1967)024<0241:TEOTAW>2.0.CO;2; 10.1175/1520-0442(1996)009<2281:DGGICC>2.0.CO;2.

motivation_short: for experiments with entangled photons, establishing the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneering quantum information science
discovery_work: D.M. Greenberger, M.A. Horne, A. Zeilinger, Going beyond Bell's theorem, in Bell's Theorem, Quantum Theory and Conceptions of the Universe (ed. M. Kafatos, Kluwer, Dordrecht), pp. 69-72 (1989)

His own experiments: first quantum teleportation, Bouwmeester et al., Nature 390, 575 (1997); entanglement swapping, Pan et al., PRL 80, 3891 (1998); Bell test under strict Einstein locality, Weihs et al., PRL 81, 5039 (1998); GHZ entanglement, Bouwmeester et al., PRL 82, 1345 (1999) and Pan et al., Nature 403, 515 (2000). note: Joint prize; anchors shared by all three laureates. This is an experimental discovery, and the two companion 1985 PRLs together are both the discovery and its first observation. The series opened with the resonant-activation method paper, Devoret, Martinis, Esteve & Clarke, PRL 53, 1260 (1984). The prediction is not by the laureates: Leggett 1978; Caldeira & Leggett, PRL 46, 211 (1981). Summary: Clarke et al., Science 239, 992 (1988). DOIs: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1543; 10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.1908.
